question: Which event has the lowest cost?
evidence: event refers to event_name; lowest cost means MIN(cost)
clarification: If several rows tie at the cut-off, return all of them.
gold: SELECT c0 FROM (SELECT T1.event_name AS c0, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY T3.cost) AS __r FROM event AS T1 INNER JOIN budget AS T2 ON T1.event_id = T2.link_to_event INNER JOIN expense AS T3 ON T2.budget_id = T3.link_to_budget) AS __t WHERE __r <= 1
gold0: SELECT T1.event_name FROM event AS T1 INNER JOIN budget AS T2 ON T1.event_id = T2.link_to_event INNER JOIN expense AS T3 ON T2.budget_id = T3.link_to_budget ORDER BY T3.cost LIMIT 1

d.request: Which event (event_name) has the lowest cost (MIN(cost)), and if multiple events tie for that lowest cost, return all of them?
d.sql: SELECT DISTINCT e.event_name FROM event e JOIN budget b ON b.link_to_event = e.event_id JOIN expense x ON x.link_to_budget = b.budget_id WHERE x.cost = (SELECT MIN(cost) FROM expense)

c.request:
Which event has the lowest cost?
Evidence: event refers to event_name; lowest cost means MIN(cost)
If several rows tie at the cut-off, return all of them.
c.sql: SELECT e.event_name FROM expense ex JOIN budget b ON ex.link_to_budget = b.budget_id JOIN event e ON b.link_to_event = e.event_id WHERE ex.cost = (SELECT MIN(cost) FROM expense)

b.request: Which event(s) have the lowest total or individual expense cost, returning the event_name of every event tied for the minimum cost value
b.sql: WITH event_cost AS (SELECT e.event_id, e.event_name, SUM(x.cost) AS total_cost FROM event e JOIN budget b ON b.link_to_event = e.event_id JOIN expense x ON x.link_to_budget = b.budget_id GROUP BY e.event_id, e.event_name) SELECT event_name FROM event_cost WHERE total_cost = (SELECT MIN(total_cost) FROM event_cost)
